title: Technology Sector Update for 11/30/2018: TIK,WDAY,ANBA,ASYS
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +0.25%
AAPL -0.53%
IBM +2.04%
CSCO +0.98%
GOOG +0.06%
Technology stocks firmed Friday afternoon, with shares of technology companies in the S&P 500 index adding over 0.8% in value today while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index spiked to a late 1.0% advance.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Tel-Instrument Electronics ( TIK ) more than doubled in price at one point on Friday before easing to roughly 60% advance after the avionics test and measurement components company received an $816,000 order from a major U.S. defense contractor for its Mode 5 test sets. The company also said the U.S. Department of Defense presented it with an AIMS certificate for its new T-47/M5 test set. The Pentagon also recently tapped Tel-Instrument for a $4.3 million test-set order.
In other sector news:
(+) Ambarella ( AMBA ) jumped over 20% at one point in recent Friday trading after the specialty chipmaker reported Q3 financial results exceeding Wall Street expectations. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.21 per share on $57.3 million in revenue compared with the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.09 per share non-GAAP profit on $57.2 million in revenue.
(+) Workday ( WDAY ) climbed more than 14% to a new record high on Friday, reaching a best-ever $166.19 a share after reporting a surprise increase in Q3 net income compared with the year-ago period. Net income for the three months ended Oct. 31 grew to $0.31 per share from $0.24 per share last year and easily beating the Capital IQ consensus expecting a year-over-year drop to $0.14 per share.
(-) Amtech Systems ( ASYS ) retreated almost 19% at one point on Friday after its fiscal Q4 net loss expanded to $0.61 per share compared with a $0.51 per share loss during the year-ago period and missing the Capital IQ consensus expecting a net loss of $0.17 per share. The solar-cell components company also is projecting fiscal Q1 revenue in a range of $27 million to $29 million, lagging the analyst mean by at least $3.1 million.
